steps.description: Load PDDL domain and problem files using unified_planning PDDLReader

suggestions: Use unified_planning.io.PDDLReader to parse PDDL files.
Load both domain and problem files: PDDLReader().parse_problem(domain_path, problem_path).
Ensure the problem object is created and valid before calling the planner.

steps.description: Generate a plan using a classical planner (e.g., pyperplan via OneshotPlanner)

suggestions: Handle the case where no plan exists (solve() returns None or status is not SOLVED_SATISFICING).
Ensure validation succeeds before saving the plan.

steps.description: Save the validated plan to disk in correct PDDL format using PDDLWriter

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ Using str(action) produces wrong PDDL format 'action(args)' instead of '(action args)'. Use PDDLWriter.write_plan() which generates correct PDDL format.
❌ Manually writing plan files bypasses PDDLWriter and produces incorrect PDDL syntax. Use unified_planning.io.PDDLWriter.write_plan() instead.
❌ Using echo to write plan files produces invalid PDDL format. Use PDDLWriter.write_plan() instead.

suggestions: CRITICAL: Use unified_planning.io.PDDLWriter.write_plan(plan, output_path) to save plans.
PDDL format requires: '(action arg1 arg2)' NOT 'action(arg1, arg2)'.
warnings: Do NOT use str(action) + newline — this produces wrong format 'move(obj)' instead of '(move obj)'.
